Test Steps: 1. Open the app URL in a fresh browser with no history. 2. Wait for the splash to finish.
Test Data: New browser profile or incognito window
Expected Result: The splash shows the Bombino branding and moves on by itself. It does not hang or need a tap to continue.

Test Steps: 1. From a fresh install swipe through every onboarding slide. 2. Press the final button.
Expected Result: Every slide is readable with no text cut off, swiping works in both directions, and the last slide leads into the app.

Test Steps: 1. Complete onboarding. 2. Close the browser tab. 3. Reopen the app URL.
Test Data: Same browser profile as the completed run
Expected Result: The app opens straight to the home screen. Onboarding is not shown a second time.

Test Steps: 1. Tap each item in the bottom bar in turn. 2. Use the browser back button after each.
Expected Result: Every tab opens its own screen, the active tab is highlighted, and back returns to the previous screen without a blank page.

Test Steps: 1. Open the side menu. 2. Follow every link in it. 3. Close the menu by tapping outside it.
Expected Result: Every link opens the right screen, and tapping outside closes the menu without navigating anywhere.

Test Steps: 1. Open home, rates, create, orders, track and profile at a phone width. 2. Scroll each to the bottom.
Expected Result: Nothing overflows sideways, no text is clipped, and every button is reachable without zooming.

Test Steps: 1. Open the same screens at a desktop width. 2. Check the sidebar and top bar.
Expected Result: The desktop sidebar and top bar appear, content is not stretched into one unreadable column, and no mobile-only chrome is left on screen.

Test Steps: 1. Type a URL that does not exist, such as /nonsense. 2. Read the screen. 3. Use the link back.
Expected Result: A friendly not-found screen appears with a way back into the app. No blank page and no raw error text.

Test Steps: 1. Set the network to offline in the browser. 2. Try to load orders and to book. 3. Restore the network.
Expected Result: The app says the connection is the problem rather than showing a blank screen, and it recovers on its own once the network returns.

Element / Feature: Phone field and Send code button
Test Steps: 1. Open /login. 2. Type the mobile number. 3. Press Send code.
Expected Result: The code is sent and the screen moves to code entry, saying which channel the code went to.

Element / Feature: Sign in with the correct code
Test Steps: 1. Request a code on a registered number. 2. Type the code. 3. Press Verify.
Test Data: Phone: 9876543210; code: the test login code from the dev team
Expected Result: Signed in and taken to the home screen, with the account name visible in the menu or profile.

Test Steps: 1. Request a code. 2. Enter a wrong code five times. 3. On the sixth try enter the correct one.
Test Data: Wrong codes 000000, 111111, 222222, 333333, 444444; then the correct code
Expected Result: Each wrong attempt shows an error. After five the code stops working even when correct, and the screen says to request a new one.

Test Steps: 1. Request a code. 2. Leave it unused for longer than its validity. 3. Enter it.
Test Data: A code left unused past its validity window
Expected Result: The screen says the code has expired, not that it is wrong, and offers to send a new one.

Test Steps: 1. Try to send a code for each value in turn.
Expected Result: The first four are refused before any code is sent. +919876543210 is either accepted as the same number or clearly refused, never sent as typed.

Test Steps: 1. Request a code for the same number ten times in two minutes.
Expected Result: The app stops sending and tells the tester to wait. It does not keep sending or fail silently.

Element / Feature: Verifying state while the code is checked
Test Steps: 1. Set the network to Slow 3G. 2. Enter the code and press Verify. 3. Try to press Verify again immediately.
Expected Result: The button shows it is working and cannot be pressed twice. The screen does not sit still with no feedback.

Element / Feature: New number goes to signup without a second code
Test Steps: 1. Enter a number that has no account. 2. Verify the code. 3. Watch what happens next and whether a second message arrives.
Expected Result: The signup screen opens with the number already filled and already verified. No second code is sent to the phone.

Test Steps: 1. Sign in. 2. Sign out from the menu or profile. 3. Reload the page and try to open /orders.
Expected Result: The user is signed out and /orders is no longer reachable without signing in again.

Element / Feature: Open a personal account, full journey
Test Steps: 1. Choose personal. 2. Enter name and email. 3. Enter the Aadhaar and PAN numbers. 4. Upload both documents. 5. Type the signature and accept the contract. 6. Submit.
Test Data: Name: Ravi Kumar; Email: ravi@example.com; Aadhaar: 234567890124; PAN: ABCDE1234F
Expected Result: The account is created, the user is signed in and lands on the home screen. Every step showed progress and nothing had to be typed twice.

Test Steps: 1. At the identity step enter the invalid number and continue. 2. Replace it with the valid one.
Expected Result: 123456789012 is refused with a message saying it is not a valid Aadhaar. 234567890124 is accepted and the step continues.

Test Steps: 1. Enter the malformed PAN and continue. 2. Replace it with a correctly shaped one.
Expected Result: The malformed value is refused with a format message. ABCDE1234F is accepted.

Test Steps: 1. Upload a clear photo to each document slot. 2. Watch the upload progress. 3. Check the slot afterwards.
Test Data: aadhaar-front.jpg and pan.jpg, both clear photos under the size limit
Expected Result: Each upload shows progress and then shows the file back with its name or a preview. The slot does not reset to empty.

Element / Feature: Wrong file type and oversized file
Test Steps: 1. Try to upload a .txt file. 2. Try to upload a very large image.
Expected Result: Both are refused with a message naming the accepted types and the size limit. The app does not hang or crash.

Element / Feature: Document that does not match the typed number
Test Steps: 1. Type a PAN number. 2. Upload a PAN document showing a different number.
Expected Result: The upload is refused as not matching the number that was typed, and the step cannot be completed until it does.

Test Steps: 1. Upload a document. 2. Remove it. 3. Upload a different one in the same slot.
Expected Result: The slot empties when removed and accepts the replacement. The old file is no longer shown anywhere.

Test Steps: 1. Open the contract preview and scroll through it. 2. Type the signatory name. 3. Accept and submit. 4. Open the signed contract from the account.
Expected Result: The contract is readable in full and the signed copy carries the typed name. Submitting with the signature blank is refused.

Element / Feature: Contract viewer on a small phone
Test Steps: 1. Set the viewport to 360 px wide. 2. Open the contract. 3. Scroll to the bottom.
Expected Result: The close button stays visible and reachable the whole time. It is never pushed off the screen by the document.

Element / Feature: Number that already has an account
Test Steps: 1. Start a signup using a number that is already registered. 2. Verify the code.
Expected Result: The app says the number already has an account and points to sign-in. It does not create a second account.

Test Steps: 1. Fill the first two steps and upload one document. 2. Close the tab. 3. Reopen the app and start signup on the same number.
Expected Result: The work already done is either still there or clearly starts fresh. Nothing half-saved is shown as complete.

Element / Feature: Open a company account, full journey
Test Steps: 1. Choose company and category corporate. 2. Enter company name, GST number, contact person and email. 3. Enter address, pincode, city, state and hub. 4. Verify the GST number. 5. Upload the GST certificate. 6. Sign and submit.
Test Data: Company: Bombino Test Exports Pvt Ltd; a real registered 15-character GST number; Pincode 400001; Hub: Mumbai
Expected Result: The account is created and signed in. The address and hub entered here are not asked for again at the first booking.

Test Steps: 1. Enter a 14-character value and continue. 2. Replace it with a well-formed but unregistered number. 3. Replace it with a real one.
Test Data: 14-char: 27AAAAA0000A1Z; unregistered: 27ZZZZZ9999Z1ZZ; then a real GST number
Expected Result: The short value gives a length message. The unregistered one is refused after the check. The real one is accepted and the company name is shown back.

Element / Feature: GST certificate must match the verified number
Test Steps: 1. Verify one GST number. 2. Upload the certificate belonging to a different company.
Test Data: Verified number for company A; certificate PDF for company B
Expected Result: The certificate is refused because the number on it does not match the one verified.

Test Steps: 1. Upload a phone photo of the certificate rather than the downloaded PDF.
Expected Result: The photo is either read and accepted, or clearly reported as unreadable with advice to upload the portal PDF. It is never silently accepted as verified.

Test Steps: 1. Choose category e-commerce. 2. Submit with the extra fields blank. 3. Fill them. 4. Switch back to corporate and submit.
Test Data: LUT number, IEC branch code, bank account number, bank AD code
Expected Result: The blank submission is refused with a message on each field. After switching to corporate those fields are no longer asked for and the values typed earlier are not carried over.

Test Steps: 1. Enter a 5-digit pincode. 2. Replace it with a valid one. 3. Submit without choosing a hub.
Expected Result: 40000 is refused. 400001 fills in Mumbai and Maharashtra by itself. Submitting with no hub is refused with Select a hub. Each field appears exactly once on the form.

Element / Feature: Book as a guest, full journey
Test Steps: 1. Open the booking screen without signing in. 2. Fill the sender name and address. 3. Verify the phone with the code. 4. Upload the KYC document asked for. 5. Complete the receiver, parcel and payment steps. 6. Submit.
Test Data: Phone: 9000000003 (no account); Pincode 400001; Weight 2 kg; Payment: Pay at pickup
Expected Result: The booking completes and the confirmation shows an order number. No account was created and no password was ever asked for.

Test Steps: 1. Start the sender step as a guest and read it from top to bottom before filling anything.
Expected Result: The address is asked for before any document is requested, and there is no empty KYC box sitting above the address.

Test Steps: 1. Enter the sender step as a guest and note what is asked first.
Expected Result: The phone is verified first. The corridor or route card does not appear on this step.

Element / Feature: Guest number that already has an account
Test Steps: 1. At the guest step enter a number that already has an account. 2. Verify the code. 3. Carry on with the booking.
Expected Result: The app signs the user into that account and continues the booking as a normal account booking, rather than treating them as a guest.

Element / Feature: Changing the phone after verifying it
Test Steps: 1. Verify one number. 2. Go back and change the sender phone to a different number. 3. Try to submit.
Expected Result: The booking is refused until the new number is verified too. The order cannot be filed against a number nobody proved.

Test Steps: 1. Upload the KYC document. 2. Stay on the step and look at the upload area. 3. Move forward a step and come back.
Expected Result: The uploaded file is shown back with its name or preview, and it is still there after leaving and returning to the step.

Element / Feature: Guest orders appear after signing up
Test Steps: 1. Book as a guest on a number. 2. Create an account on the same number. 3. Open the orders screen.
Expected Result: Every order booked as a guest on that number now appears in the account's order list.

Test Steps: 1. Read the heading on the guest step. 2. Change the destination and read it again.
Test Data: Destination USA, then another available destination
Expected Result: The heading matches the destination actually chosen. It does not name a fixed country regardless of the selection.

Test Steps: 1. Enter origin, destination, weight and dimensions. 2. Press Calculate. 3. Note the amount. 4. Price the same parcel through the booking screen.
Test Data: Origin 400001; Destination USA; Weight 2 kg; Dimensions 30 x 20 x 15 cm
Expected Result: A rate is shown with a readable breakdown, and the booking screen quotes the same amount for the same parcel.

Test Steps: 1. Calculate with each value in turn.
Expected Result: 0 and -1 are refused with a message. 9999 either quotes or explains the limit. No blank, NaN or negative amount is ever shown.

Test Steps: 1. Quote a light but large parcel. 2. Read which weight the breakdown says was charged.
Test Data: Weight 1 kg; Dimensions 60 x 50 x 40 cm
Expected Result: The breakdown says the volumetric weight was used and explains why the price is higher than 1 kg would suggest.

Test Steps: 1. Fill the sender step. 2. Fill the receiver step. 3. Fill the parcel step. 4. Choose Pickup, a date and a payment method. 5. Submit. 6. Open the orders screen.
Test Data: Sender pincode 400001; Weight 2 kg; Pickup today; Payment: Pay at pickup
Expected Result: The booking completes, a confirmation with an order number is shown, and the order appears in the orders list straight away.

Test Steps: 1. Follow the same journey but choose Drop-off. 2. Submit.
Expected Result: The booking completes without ever asking for a pickup date or an agent, and the confirmation explains where to bring the parcel.

Element / Feature: Pickup date before the local cutoff
Test Steps: 1. Before 3 PM IST enter the pincode at the pickup step. 2. Open the date picker.
Expected Result: Today can be chosen as the pickup date.

Element / Feature: Pickup date after the local cutoff
Test Steps: 1. At or after 3 PM IST enter the same pincode. 2. Open the date picker.
Test Data: Pincode 700001 (Kolkata); tested at or after 3 PM IST
Expected Result: Today can no longer be chosen and the earliest date is tomorrow. The screen explains why.

Test Steps: 1. At around 4 PM IST enter the Mumbai Fort pincode and open the date picker. 2. Change to the Delhi pincode. 3. Change to the Kolkata pincode.
Test Data: 400001 Fort; 110059 Delhi; 700001 Kolkata; tested about 4 PM IST
Expected Result: Fort and Delhi still offer today at 4 PM. Kolkata does not. The date offered follows the collecting city, not one fixed time for the whole country.

Element / Feature: Pickup where no agent covers the area
Test Steps: 1. Enter a covered pincode and note the delivery options. 2. Replace it with an uncovered one. 3. Try to choose Pickup anyway.
Expected Result: 400001 offers doorstep pickup. 560001 does not, drop-off is offered instead, and the screen says why rather than just greying the option out.

Test Steps: 1. Enter the last pincode inside the Hyderabad area. 2. Then the first one outside it.
Expected Result: 500089 offers pickup. 500090 does not and falls back to drop-off. Neither shows an error.

Element / Feature: Extra charge notice outside the normal beat
Test Steps: 1. Enter a Kolkata pincode marked as outside the city beat. 2. Read the notice. 3. Continue the booking.
Expected Result: A notice warns that an extra charge applies, without quoting a figure, and the booking is still allowed to go ahead.

Test Steps: 1. At the parcel step choose Pack it for me instead of Already packed. 2. Submit. 3. Open the order.
Expected Result: The choice is shown on the confirmation and on the order, so the customer can see the request was recorded.

Test Steps: 1. On each of the four steps clear the required fields and press Continue.
Test Data: All required fields left blank in turn
Expected Result: Each step refuses to advance and marks exactly which fields are missing. The step is not ticked off as done.

Test Steps: 1. Type the valid pincode in the address. 2. Then type an unassigned one.
Expected Result: 400001 fills in Mumbai and Maharashtra. 999999 says it was not found and the form can still be completed by typing the city manually.

Test Steps: 1. Fill steps one to three. 2. Go back to step one. 3. Return forward to step three.
Test Data: Any complete sender, receiver and parcel data
Expected Result: Everything typed is still there. Nothing is silently cleared by moving backwards.

Element / Feature: Booking on an account with documents missing
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as an account with a document missing or flagged. 2. Try to book.
Test Data: Account with one document flagged by ops
Expected Result: The booking is blocked and the banner says exactly which document is missing and where to upload it.

Test Steps: 1. On a company account reach the last step. 2. Choose Bond UT and submit. 3. Book again choosing IGST.
Test Data: Company account; Bond UT, then IGST
Expected Result: Both choices are accepted and each is shown back on its own order.

Test Steps: 1. Fill a booking completely. 2. Press Submit twice quickly. 3. Open the orders screen.
Test Data: Any valid booking; two rapid presses
Expected Result: Exactly one order is created. The orders list does not show the same booking twice.

Test Steps: 1. Choose Pay Now. 2. Complete the payment with the test card. 3. Open the order.
Test Data: Test card 4111 1111 1111 1111 with any future expiry
Expected Result: The payment succeeds and the order shows as paid, with the amount matching the quote.

Test Steps: 1. Choose Pay Now. 2. Use the card that forces a failure. 3. Read the screen and check the order.
Test Data: The Razorpay test card that declines
Expected Result: The screen says the payment failed and offers to try again. The order is not shown as paid.

Test Steps: 1. Choose Pay Now. 2. Close the payment window without paying. 3. Return to the app.
Expected Result: The app returns to the booking with the order unpaid and a clear way to pay again. It does not freeze on a loading screen.

Test Steps: 1. Book choosing Pay at pickup. 2. Read the confirmation. 3. Open the order.
Expected Result: The confirmation and the order both say the amount will be collected at pickup, and the amount is shown.

Test Steps: 1. Book choosing Pay at drop-off. 2. Read the confirmation.
Expected Result: The confirmation says the amount is payable at the drop-off point and names the amount.

Test Steps: 1. Book with COD. 2. Open the order and the orders list.
Expected Result: The order is marked COD in both places, using the same wording.

Test Steps: 1. Open an unpaid pay-now order from the list. 2. Pay from the order screen.
Expected Result: The payment can be completed from the order itself and the status changes to paid without rebooking.

Test Steps: 1. Open the orders screen on an account with several orders. 2. Read the status on each card.
Test Data: Account with orders in several stages
Expected Result: Every order is listed with a status a customer can understand. No internal codes such as ready_for_docket are shown.

Test Steps: 1. Sign in as a brand-new account. 2. Open the orders screen.
Expected Result: A friendly empty state explains there are no orders yet and offers a way to book. Not a blank screen or a spinner that never stops.

Test Steps: 1. Open an order from the list. 2. Read every section.
Expected Result: Sender, receiver, parcel, payment method, payment status and the tracking timeline are all filled in with real values. No blank fields or placeholder text.

Test Steps: 1. Enter a real AWB and search. 2. Then enter a made-up one.
Test Data: A real AWB from a dispatched order; then ZZ999999999ZZ
Expected Result: The real AWB shows its timeline in the right order. The made-up one shows a not-found message, not an error page or an endless spinner.

Test Steps: 1. Open an order that has not been picked up. 2. Request cancellation. 3. Read the order afterwards.
Expected Result: The request is accepted and the order says a cancellation is pending review. The customer is not told it is already cancelled.

Test Steps: 1. Open an order that has already been dispatched. 2. Look for the cancel option.
Expected Result: There is no cancel option, and if one is shown it explains that the order has gone too far to cancel.

Test Steps: 1. Open an order that has documents. 2. Open each document.
Test Data: An order with an uploaded KYC document and a signed contract
Expected Result: Each document opens and is readable. Nothing belonging to another customer is ever listed here.

Test Steps: 1. Note the unread badge. 2. Open the notifications screen. 3. Read one notification. 4. Look at the badge again.
Expected Result: Notifications are listed newest first and the badge count drops by one after reading one.

Test Steps: 1. Book an order. 2. Have ops or an agent move it through two stages. 3. Open notifications.
Test Data: One order moved from booked to picked up
Expected Result: A notification appears for each stage, worded for a customer, and tapping one opens the order it refers to.

Test Steps: 1. Book an order on a number with WhatsApp. 2. Check the phone.
Test Data: A phone number with WhatsApp active
Expected Result: A WhatsApp message about the booking arrives. If it does not, the in-app notification is still there, so nothing is lost.

Test Steps: 1. Open the profile screen. 2. Check the name, phone, email and account type.
Expected Result: Everything shown matches what was entered at signup. No field is blank or shows a placeholder.

Test Steps: 1. Change the account phone to a new number. 2. Verify the new number. 3. Sign out and try to sign in with the old number.
Expected Result: The new number needs its own code and then works. The old number no longer signs in to that account.

Test Steps: 1. Open the documents section of the profile. 2. Check each slot and its status.
Test Data: Account with documents uploaded at signup
Expected Result: Each document is listed with its verification status, and a rejected one can be replaced.

Test Steps: 1. Open support. 2. Ask a question. 3. Ask a follow-up. 4. Start a new session.
Test Data: Question: How do I track my shipment?
Expected Result: An answer comes back, the follow-up is understood in context, and New session clears the conversation.

Test Steps: 1. Send fifteen messages in under a minute.
Expected Result: The app asks the tester to slow down with a clear message. It does not hang or lose the conversation.

Test Steps: 1. Open the privacy page from the menu. 2. Scroll to the bottom.
Expected Result: The page loads in full and is readable on a phone. No missing sections or broken links.
